steps.text: The aging general stands silently in the tent, like a brick on an ancient wall.
Behind him is the military map that he has drawn a thousand times in his mind. Before him is the faint silhouette of Baizao.
The rain of the heartlands is unfamiliar to one used to the sands of the frontier. The clouds hang low, suffocatingly so.
The general's thoughts drift away.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: You are the new commander of Yumen, I take it.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: You can call me Shuo. My responsibility is to assist you in military matters, as well as kung fu instruction for the soldiers.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: I can take you around the base, if you'd like.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You don't remember me?

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: I saw your name in the imperial court's announcement... what do you mean by 'remember'?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Never mind.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I don't need a guide. I've served in Yumen before.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: I see. Forgive my impudence.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: It seems we are old comrades.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: The memories tend to fade after all these years on the border. Forgive me, if I've caused any offense.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Memories faded, I see... interesting.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Get yourself warmed up. I want to spar.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: You've had a long journey. You should rest; I would be happy to spar with you another day.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I don't need to rest.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I want to get some exercise before dinner.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: We should go no further, General.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: The supply lines and the troops' morale have been stretched to the limit.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: We cannot afford to be reckless when fighting demons. To push forward would be very risky.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: We're so close...!

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: It's already a remarkable victory, General.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: The demons of the north feed on the fear in men's hearts... this is the first time I've seen a general press on without fear, even with the entire army's fate upon your shoulders.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: There is nothing to fear!

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: These things have harmed our people, ruined cities and farms... I only wish we could have wiped them out in this battle!

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Give me twenty years, I swear, I will see all the demons wiped out!

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: I have no doubt you will, sir.

steps.name: Shuo
steps.text: I doubt anything under heaven could daunt you.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: What about you?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: You seem indomitable, invincible...

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Have you ever been afraid?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Transfer?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: My appointment to Yumen was for a hundred years. It's time to leave.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: And the Sui Regulator didn't tell me anything about the personnel change? They are getting more and more out of line.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: But why are you leaving now? Trouble is stirring in the northwest. We need you more than ever.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Perhaps our time together has made you forget...

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I've never held any official position in Yumen.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Where are you going? Danyan? Michu?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: I think I will be stepping away, fully, from my responsibilities.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: Communications from the Candleholders watching the Tomb of Sui have become increasingly frequent. Its awakening approaches.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: It would not be appropriate for me to shoulder important responsibilities at this time.

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: But Yumen is strong and well-equipped. It will perform its duty well, whether protecting Great Yan's northwestern border, or any other purpose.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Where are you going, after you leave?

steps.name: Chongyue
steps.text: The jianghu world is big. There are plenty of places to go.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: ...Report.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Have the scouts returned?

steps.name: Yumen Sentry
steps.text: Not yet, sir.

steps.name: Yumen Sentry
steps.text: And we have received no instructions from Baizao in the past three days.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: The Sui Regulator should be communicating with Yumen, regardless of what is happening in the Tomb of Sui...

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Send out messengers—

steps.name: Yumen Sentry
steps.text: Sir! They're forcing their way in!

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: What is the meaning of this?

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: General Zuo.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: It is most irregular to invade my tent like this, even for the military supervisory censor.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: On whose orders are you operating?

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: The Grand Commandant has sent me to question you on the unnecessary delay.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Ridiculous!

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Yumen has been on full alert since it received the order to mobilize. There has been no delay!

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: Have you forgotten that Yumen received orders to arrive at Baizao by the last day of July at the beginning of the year, but arrived three days late? What is this, if not a delay?

steps.name: Yumen Sentry
steps.text: Yumen was struck by a Catastrophe at the beginning of the year, and the repairs took two months! The imperial court must have known—

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Silence!

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Hmph... I take responsibility for Yumen's delay.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Did you come to strip me of command, then?

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: You know the Grand Commandant thinks highly of you.

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: But it seems, now, that you do not trust the Grand Commandant.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Such words are inappropriate for a solemn place like this.

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: Kindly instruct Yumen to travel twenty li in the direction of the Tomb of Sui.

spans.text: Kindly instruct Yumen to travel twenty
in the direction of the Tomb of Sui.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Yumen is already as close as it is allowed to be under standby. Why should we approach any closer?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: The situation in the Tomb of Sui is yet unclear. Are you saying that Yumen should attack?

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: Your duty is to obey. There is no need to question.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: What is His Imperial Majesty's will?

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: Are you questioning your orders, General Zuo?

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: I cannot abide such questionable orders!

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: If you will not accept your orders, then I must ask you to leave this tent.

steps.name: Yumen Sentry
steps.text: How dare you!

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: Stop!

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: My presence here represents the will of the Grand Commandant.

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: All you need to do is obey. Even if His Imperial Majesty questions, he can find no fault in your actions.

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: The bestial Sui is awakening. War is inevitable. Do you still intend to defy orders and paralyze Yumen with inaction?

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: We are at a crisis. The lives of millions hinge on your decision—including your wife and son, who are still in the Baizao city.

steps.name: Zuo Xuanliao
steps.text: How dare you?!

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: Not us. You, General.

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: According to the estimates of the Ministry of War, Baizao will be doomed as long as you continue to defy orders, and Yumen remains unmoving.

steps.name: Military Supervisory Censor
steps.text: There is no time. We will wait here until you have come to a decision.
Does it look familiar?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: It has changed, but it is still recognizable as the court that judges all matters under Heaven.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Why have you come back at this time, when you have not done so for so many years?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: I have an appointment I cannot miss.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: But you took the time to come to the Judicial Review Office. Did you want to see if your successors have disappointed you?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: My views are insignificant. The Judicial Review Office should only think about not disappointing the people of Yan.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: One of the deputy ministers resigned recently. It's a shame—you would have liked her.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: I hope she didn't resign because she was disappointed.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Hard to say...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Do you still play the guqin?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Never forget the five sounds, for that they ensure proper virtue.' I have also been trying out new instruments recently.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I see... more pleasant than studying the Laws of Yan, I expect.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: It is an interesting discipline.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I read the Basic Principles of the Laws of Yan that you left behind many times, but I could never understand the last third.

spans.text: Basic Principles of the Laws of Yan
that you left behind many times, but I could never understand the last third.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: I spent so much time studying it that I almost failed my Ministry of Justice entrance exam. Maybe I would have become a Candleholder.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: It took many years for me to understand... the justice that you wrote about lay beyond the mortal realm.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Just as one cannot draw what one has never seen, one cannot write about conscience that does not exist in their hearts.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: If justice is nowhere to be seen in the mortal realm, then one must consider—has someone blinded our eyes?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You still bear a grudge for what happened back then.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Should I not?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: What about the people who died in the turmoil? The innocent souls who were dragged into the game? Should they bear a grudge against him?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Yes, they should.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Then how do you seek a fair judgment for it?

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: You forget.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Not one law of Yan was written for the sole purpose of resolving hatred.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: It is someone else who should be judged.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Looks like you're not worried about what will happen to your brother in the Tomb of Sui. You're more worried about the judgment he'll receive.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Justice has never been concerned with life and death. He and I seek different things.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: You're right, but at a time like this... I can't help but feel...

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: Law and regulations were written by humans, but the supreme law in your heart that transcends the strife of the mortal realm... may never be found there.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: But just this once... if the time comes that we put the sinner on trial, I will put you in the judge's chair.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: You're correct.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: And it's been a long time since I judged anyone.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: I take my leave.

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: There's no rush, is there? Join me in a cup of mortal tea before you leave.

steps.name: Jun
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Chen Che
steps.text: It takes mortal hands to make and serve the best mortal tea, after all.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: The Sky Mirror Pavilion is bigger than I thought... that's the sealed room on the top floor, right?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: How about someone knocks on the door and figures out how to open it?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: There's no one here. I think we're the first.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: There is one thing that I don't quite understand, Zuo Le.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: If the Grand Commandant is after the proxy's relic, I take it that he knows how to use it to neutralize the bestial Sui?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: He is one of the three Grand Ministers. If he made plans to obtain it, then he has certainly made plans to use it.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: I even find myself wondering... if someone takes the opportunity to erase another proxy's name with the writing knife while Wang is fighting Sui...

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But what does all this have to do with Wei Yenwu?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: The Grand Commandant wouldn't have needed the writing knife if he was that powerful. He could have gone into the Tomb of Sui and killed Sui with his own bare hands.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: What ideas do YOU have, then?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: I didn't really care about you and your official stuff, but I have a pretty good idea what's going on after listening to you guys talk.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Basically, the crown prince who went missing forty years ago after being suspected of staging a coup is back. Am I right?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Do not speak of it so casually!

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Gah, I'm not wasting my time arguing with you.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Basically, there's another direct descendant of the True Lung here in Baizao. That explains everything.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: What are you getting at?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Have you never heard of the special Originium under Baizao used to suppress Sui?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Miss Ch'en here is from Lungmen, so it's understandable that she doesn't know. But you two should... unless it's above your rank?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: Do you mean...?

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: 'The Earth's blessings have granted this stone to its people; the Heaven's blessings shall bring an end to Sui.'

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: A legend associated with the Great Hunt. I thought it was a myth, maybe some kind of allegory...

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: All I know is that the Tomb of Sui was built around a special facility...

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: Alright, I guess you don't know.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Why do YOU know?

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: I guess the Sui Regulator left no record of who gave Yan this Originium either.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: It was our grandmaster, Ju's first friend, and the first Shanhaizhong.

steps.name: Mo Yi
steps.text: To be precise, it was a personal gift to the True Lung. Meaning—

steps.name: Ch'en Chao-ch'ien
steps.text: What happened?

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Looks like the evacuation of the civilians is complete, and the plates are beginning to separate.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: Time is short. We should retrieve—
So you really made it here.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Who's—
A figure approaches them from the other side of the corridor.

steps.name: Zuo Le
steps.text: You... but how could it be—

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: All districts have been fully evacuated, Your Imperial Majesty, and all the ministries are ready.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: They await your command.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Tomorrow is the day of the full moon.

steps.name: Imperial Guard
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Very well.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: Separate the plates.
Heaven and earth rumble in the setting golden sun.
The plates of Baizao begin to separate, starting from the outer areas, casting numerous shadows in the vast wilderness.
They are the legs that carry the city, and the foundation of its existence—
Shanshui, Changjie, Yanhuo, Xiange;
Duanfang, Baigu, Zaifu, Bingge...
The Eight Districts have seen a hundred springs and autumns together.
They have long been standing united, overcoming hardships.
Now that they are separated, the future is uncertain.

steps.name: True Lung
steps.text: I was wondering when you would come.

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: Your Imperial Majesty...

steps.name: Grand Commandant
steps.text: It is time.
